kaps_punt: Maniere waarop mense in hulle behoeftes voorsien: Stories om te beskryf hoe mense in verskillende plekke in hulle behoeftes voorsien ****

items.bewering: Alle mense het dieselfde basiese behoeftes, en water en kos is twee daarvan.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: World Vision Canada, 'The same, but different. What are basic needs and how do we meet them?' (worldvision.ca): water, food and shelter are basic needs shared by everyone, and the ways people meet them differ. Lists of basic needs vary from source to source, but every one of them includes water and food, and the lesson only claims that these two are among them.

items.bewering: Water kom op meer as een manier by 'n huis uit. Die algemeenste manier is 'n kraan binne die huis.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/65845), reporting Census 2022: 59.7% of households have piped water inside the dwelling, the largest single category, up from 46.3% in 2011. The same split (59.7% inside, 22.7% in the yard, 8.9% at a community tap) appears in the Eastern Cape Treasury's Estimates of Provincial Revenue and Expenditure 2025/26, p. 34, citing Stats SA. This holds for South Africa as a whole, which is how the lesson frames it. It does not hold in every province: in Limpopo only 31.4% have a tap inside. The sentence makes no provincial claim, so nothing needs to change.

items.bewering: Baie ander huise het 'n eie kraan buite in die jaart.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: Census 2022 via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/65845): 82.4% have piped water inside the dwelling or in the yard, and 59.7% inside, so about 22.7% have a tap in the yard only. The Eastern Cape Treasury EPRE 2025/26, p. 34 gives 22.7% in the yard. This is the second-largest group, which fits 'baie ander'.

items.bewering: Nog minder gesinne haal hul water by 'n gemeenskapskraan wat baie gesinne deel.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: Census 2022 via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/65845): off-site access (a neighbour's tap or a community stand) was 8.9% in 2022, down from 17.9% in 2011. The Eastern Cape Treasury EPRE 2025/26, p. 34 gives 8.9% for community taps nationally. This is fewer than the roughly 22.7% with a yard tap, so the order the lesson gives (inside, then yard, then communal tap) is right.

items.bewering: Party gesinne kry hul water nie uit die munisipaliteit se waterpype nie. Hulle haal dit byvoorbeeld uit 'n boorgat, 'n rivier of 'n reënwatertenk.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: Stats SA General Household Survey, 'main source of drinking water' variable, as listed in the DataFirst catalogue at UCT (datafirst.uct.ac.za, catalog 1027 V625 and catalog 945 V30). Its categories include a borehole on site and off site, a rainwater tank on site, and flowing water/stream/river, alongside the piped categories. Census 2022 via SAnews: households with no piped water at all, up to 20.5% in Limpopo.

items.bewering: Daar is dae waarop die water nie by die huise uitkom nie.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: Helen Suzman Foundation brief, 'Water quality, reliability and payment for services: household perspectives II' (hsf.org.za), analysing the 2018 GHS: 41.7% of households supplied by municipalities had a water interruption in the previous 12 months. EWN, 13 September 2025: Johannesburg outages lasting a week.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense koop die meeste van hul kos by winkels.
items.blok: Almal het water en kos nodig
items.bron: Stats SA GHS 2023, as reported by East Coast Radio (ecr.co.za): only 11.7% of households named small-scale agriculture as their main source of food. Even in rural areas, Ngidi (2007), UKZN MSc thesis, hdl.handle.net/10413/3446, found that more than 80% of the food households in Umbumbulu and Maphephetheni, KwaZulu-Natal, consumed was bought, with 4% and 13% from their own production. Both stories repeat this sentence ('Die gesin koop die meeste van hul kos by winkels'), and it holds there too, including for the rural family.

items.bewering: Thabo woon op die platteland. ... Pype bring water tot by die gesin se eie kraan in die jaart. Binne die huis is daar geen kraan nie. Op party dae loop die jaartkraan droog. Dan stap die gesin ver na 'n gemeenskapskraan en dra die water in emmers huis toe.
items.bron: This is a typical case, not a statistic. In rural provinces a tap inside the house is less common (Limpopo 31.4% inside the dwelling, per Census 2022 via SAnews), so a yard tap with none inside fits. Haarhoff & Rietveld (2009), 'Public standpipe design and maintenance for rural South Africa' (ircwash.org): the public standpipe is the user interface of most rural water systems in South Africa. HSF/GHS 2018: interruptions are common. A yard tap failing while a communal tap still runs is plausible, because rural standpipes are often on separate borehole-fed schemes. The story only says what this one family does.

items.bewering: Die gesin se baksteenhuis hou hulle droog en veilig.
items.bron: World Vision Canada, 'What are basic needs and how do we meet them?' (worldvision.ca): shelter is a basic need, and it means protection from the weather and from danger. The sentence describes one family's house and makes no wider claim. The same sentence appears in 'Aisha in 'n besige dorp'.

items.bewering: Drie klein winkels naby die huis verkoop brood, melk en seep. ... Die kliniek, die skool en daardie winkels is naby genoeg om soontoe te loop. Die gesin se naaste hospitaal is ver weg in 'n groter dorp.
items.bron: Daily Maverick / Spotlight, 11 November 2018, 'Mankosi clinic: the long and winding road to rural healthcare': in a village near Mthatha the nearest hospital is about 30 km away. Sowetan, 23 March 2021, 'Healthcare woes for remote Vhembe villages'. Rural hospitals in South Africa sit in larger towns and clinics serve the villages, which matches the story. Small shops near the home selling bread, milk and soap are ordinary in rural South Africa. This is a story detail about one family and no general claim is made.

items.bewering: Minibus-taxi's op die gruispaaie neem mense soontoe en na ander plekke wat verder weg is.
items.bron: National Household Travel Survey 2020, DataFirst catalogue 886 (datafirst.uct.ac.za): minibus taxis are the public transport mode most households report using. Most of South Africa's road network is gravel, at roughly 79% (dnaeconomics.com, 'Gravel roads in a wetter future'). Some remote villages have no taxi service at all (Sowetan 2021, Vhembe), but the story is about one place that does and does not claim every village has one.

items.bewering: Maar die gruispaaie word modderig as dit reën en stowwerig as dit droog is.
items.bron: AFCAP / research4cap.org, Mtawali (2010), 'Access challenges on unpaved roads', Malawi: in the dry season traffic and dry weather produce dust and corrugations, and in the rainy season mud pools and slippery surfaces. Greening et al. (2010), AFCAP overview of dust on unpaved roads. dnaeconomics.com, on South African gravel roads: moisture brings erosion, potholes and slipperiness, and some roads become impassable after rain.

items.bewering: Pype bring water tot by die gesin se eie kraan in die kombuis. Op party dae loop daardie kraan droog. Dan bring 'n munisipale watervragmotor water, en die gesin dra dit in emmers huis toe.
items.bron: EWN, 13 September 2025, 'Water tankers bring relief after week-long outages in parts of Joburg'. EWN, 15 March 2024: the City of Johannesburg uses about 60 water tankers a day to bring emergency drinking water to residents during outages. Allafrica, August 2024, 'Ten years on and households still rely on water trucks' (KwaZulu-Natal). Families collecting water from a tanker in containers is the way it is distributed.

items.bewering: Haar dorp het self 'n hospitaal. Minibus-taxi's op die geteerde strate neem mense na plekke wat verder weg is. Maar diep slaggate in die strate laat die verkeer stadig ry.
items.bron: The Citizen / Sandton Chronicle, 29 December 2025: deep potholes in Kew, Johannesburg force drivers to slow down or swerve. Thepost.co.za, 23 April 2025: the AA estimates more than 25 million potholes on South African roads. NHTS 2020 (DataFirst catalogue 886): minibus taxis are the main public transport. A larger town having its own hospital is ordinary, and this is a story detail.

items.bewering: Read as a set: the two stories side by side. The rural family has a yard tap, a far-off hospital and gravel roads that turn muddy or dusty. The town family has a kitchen tap, its own hospital and tarred streets with potholes. Both families buy most of their food at shops, live in a brick house, and walk to school, a clinic and shops.
items.blok: Thabo op die platteland / Aisha in 'n besige dorp
items.bron: Checked as a comparison, for what the contrast teaches. Every difference the stories draw points the way the national data does: inside taps are less common in rural provinces (Census 2022 via SAnews, Limpopo 31.4% against 59.7% nationally), rural hospitals sit in larger towns (Daily Maverick/Spotlight 2018), and most of the road network outside towns is gravel (dnaeconomics.com). The things the two families share are also true in both settings, notably buying most food (Ngidi 2007, UKZN, for rural KZN; GHS 2023 nationally) and water outages (HSF/GHS 2018; EWN 2025). Neither story is presented as the only way of life in its setting, so a learner reasoning further is not led to a false generalisation. One small point a person may like to know, and it is not an error: a learner could take it that town streets are always tarred and country roads always gravel. Both are true as a typical pattern, and the stories show one family each.

items.bewering: gemeenskapskraan: 'n Openbare kraan in die straat of op oop grond wat baie gesinne van 'n gemeenskap deel.
items.bron: Stats SA's GHS category 'Public/communal tap' (DataFirst catalogue 1027 V625) and Census 2022's 'community stand' (SAnews). Wikipedia, 'Standpipe (street)': a freestanding outdoor pipe with a tap, used as a communal supply where homes have no piped water of their own. Haarhoff & Rietveld (2009), ircwash.org: public standpipes serve whole rural communities. Allafrica 2024: communal standpipes once supplied about 1,000 households in Mandeni. The definition is accurate, and simple without becoming false.

opsomming: All 16 claims hold up against South African sources. That includes the one superlative, that a tap inside the house is the most common way water reaches a home, which is true nationally per Census 2022 (59.7% inside, about 22.7% in the yard, 8.9% at a communal tap). Two things are worth a person's eye but need no change: that superlative is national and does not hold in every province (Limpopo is 31.4%), and the sentence makes no provincial claim; the lesson contains no eli10 block.
